[LSIG.2.2.4] **Window convention.** The window is the half-open interval
`(t−W, t]`: the left boundary `t−W` is exclusive and the right boundary `t`
is inclusive. The runtime must apply this convention consistently across
every `SeriesBackendIntervalPulse` query path and every conformance fixture. The same convention
governs `onset_rate`'s edge count (§[LSIG.1.4]) so that the two compose over
identical bounds.

tla.name: lsig_2_2_4__edges_share_the_sample_window
tla.note: EDGES SHARE THE SAMPLE WINDOW, within the scope: under `sliding`, the edges a read counts in its window are exactly the edges among the samples it sees, so the edge count and the window compose over one half-open bound; a closed bound applied to edges alone is refused (`.teeth.edge_closed`). The convention on the samples themselves, a sample exactly W old outside and the closed bound refused, is `lser_14_1__read_sees_the_window`'s, and `.probe.boundary` shows the boundary case reached. The `SeriesBackendIntervalPulse` query paths and the fixtures the clause names are not modelled; the model states one window for one instance.
